The piece is presented with the before and after images side by side, the scope statement is walked through item by item including the out-of-scope entries so the remaining scratch or the untouched clasp is seen and understood as agreed rather than discovered later, the small-part and stone counts are reconciled against intake, the retained colour reference is compared under the light it was agreed in, and the wear expectation and care sheet are restated and handed over in writing. The client inspects and signs acceptance; if they are not satisfied, that is captured in the same moment while the evidence is fresh rather than becoming a complaint weeks later. Nothing at handover describes the work as making the piece solid gold, and no durability guarantee is added verbally to close a hesitant collection. The complete file — ticket, photos before and after, signed sheet, gate passes, discovery records and the acceptance signature — is retained as one unit under the shop's stated retention and privacy practice, which is what makes any later dispute decidable.

included: the guided inspection against scope and images
count reconciliation and colour reference comparison
acceptance signature and retention of the complete job file
excluded: technical quality release of the deposit, owned by the finish-quality specialist
invoicing and payment terms
trade parcel return logistics, owned by the trade-account knowledge base

pros.claim: Walking the out-of-scope list at collection converts the commonest complaint into a shared observation
pros.example: showing the client the scratch they chose to keep, next to its intake photo, before they leave the shop

pros.claim: A complete retained file makes any later claim decidable from evidence rather than memory
pros.example: a claim three months on answered in minutes from the file's before and after pair and the signed sheet

cons.claim: A guided handover takes counter time and can feel like the shop is pre-arguing a dispute
cons.example: a delighted client kept at the counter through an inspection they did not want

cons.claim: Retaining complete files creates a personal-data duty that must be defined and honoured
cons.example: years of client images and contact details held with no stated retention period in a jurisdiction whose privacy rules must be checked

failure_modes: handing over in a bag with no inspection because the shop is busy
letting a verbal durability promise slip out to close a hesitant collection
an incomplete file where the gate passes or the after images were never attached
acceptance_tests: every collected job has an acceptance signature and an after image set comparable to its before set
the retained file contains ticket, before and after images, signed sheet, gate passes, any discovery records and the acceptance record, under the shop's stated retention practice
revisit_triggers: a complaint arrives that the file cannot resolve
privacy or retention obligations in the shop's jurisdiction change
handover volume makes the guided inspection impractical as designed

base.update_signal: a complaint the retained file could not settle, or a change in retention and privacy obligations

nodes.definition: Hand over written care guidance because the wearer's habits are one of the largest variables in how long the finish looks new, and because a client who was never told cannot be expected to have known. The sheet explains the mechanism rather than issuing rules for their own sake: a thin coating is abraded by contact and attacked by chemistry, so pieces are removed before swimming, cleaning, gardening, gym work and heavy manual tasks; lotions, perfumes, hair products and hand sanitiser are applied before the piece goes on rather than over it; storage is separate and soft so pieces do not abrade each other in a box; cleaning is a soft dry or barely damp cloth rather than an abrasive polish, a dip solution or a household cleaner, since polishing compounds remove the very layer that was just applied; and a piece worn daily on a working hand will show contact wear first no matter how it is cared for. It also tells the client what to do when wear appears, which is to come back for a refresh, and what not to do, which is to have it buffed by someone who will thin it further.

included: the care mechanism given in writing at handover
what to do when wear appears and what to avoid
storage and cleaning guidance appropriate to a coated piece
excluded: cleaning or restoration services performed by the shop
medical guidance on skin reactions, which routes to regulation classes and a clinician
chemical product recommendations beyond avoiding abrasives and aggressive cleaners

pros.claim: Written care guidance removes the commonest cause of premature wear and the argument that follows it
pros.example: a client who would have worn the piece in a chlorinated pool every morning learning why not, in writing, at collection

pros.claim: Telling the client to return when wear appears turns the coating's finite life into an expected revisit rather than a grievance
pros.example: a client booking a refresh at a year rather than complaining that the finish failed

cons.claim: Care instructions can read as a pre-emptive excuse if they are not paired with the shop's own accountability
cons.example: a complaint answered only by pointing at the care sheet when the real cause was a process defect

cons.claim: Clients rarely follow care advice fully, so it manages expectation more than it changes behaviour
cons.example: a daily-worn ring going through hand washing dozens of times a week regardless of any sheet

failure_modes: issuing generic jewellery care wording that ignores what a coating specifically cannot tolerate
using the care sheet as the default answer to every complaint
giving the guidance verbally at a busy counter and never in writing
acceptance_tests: every collected customer piece leaves with the written care sheet, and the file records that it was given
the care sheet explains the mechanism behind each instruction rather than listing bare rules
revisit_triggers: wear complaints cluster on a behaviour the sheet does not address
the shop changes deposit type so the appropriate care changes
the sheet is being used as the standard complaint response

base.update_signal: a complaint pattern tied to a care behaviour the sheet does not cover, or a change in deposit type that changes appropriate care

nodes.definition: Handle a returning client with a decision procedure rather than a mood, since the same complaint can be a genuine process defect, ordinary wear that was disclosed, or damage from use, and each deserves a different answer. The sequence is to receive the piece back under the same custody and photography discipline as a new intake, compare against the retained before and after images and the signed scope, and classify: adhesion loss, missed or unplated areas, burn or staining, trapped solution bleed and colour far outside the agreed reference point at the shop's process; uniform thinning at contact zones on a piece worn daily points at the disclosed wear mechanism; and impact damage, chemical attack or abrasive cleaning show their own signatures. A defect is redone or refunded without argument and the cause is fed back to the bench specialists; disclosed wear is explained against the client's own signed disclosure with a re-plate offered as the normal cycle; ambiguous cases are resolved in the client's favour once, with the reason recorded so the pattern is visible. Every outcome updates something upstream — the refusal list, the survey, the disclosure wording or the care sheet — because a complaint that changes nothing will simply return.

included: re-intake of a returned piece under full custody and photo discipline
classifying defect versus disclosed wear versus use damage from evidence
the resolve-once-in-the-client's-favour rule for ambiguity and the upstream feedback duty
excluded: diagnosing the bench cause of a defect, which the finish-quality specialist owns
statutory consumer-rights determinations in the shop's market
trade-account credit notes and account-level remedies

pros.claim: Classifying from retained evidence keeps the answer consistent whether the client is calm or furious
pros.example: uniform thinning on the underside of a daily-worn shank read against the disclosure rather than against the volume of the complaint

pros.claim: Feeding every outcome upstream turns individual complaints into a shrinking failure class
pros.example: three trapped-solution complaints on hollow pieces adding a hollow-form handling decision to the intake survey

cons.claim: Resolving ambiguity in the client's favour can be exploited and costs real gold and bench time
cons.example: a client returning repeatedly with wear on a piece they wear through heavy manual work

cons.claim: Evidence-based classification is only as good as the retained record, so old jobs with thin files stay arguable
cons.example: a complaint on a job taken in before the shop photographed defects at macro range

failure_modes: arguing from memory or from the loudest voice rather than from the file
defaulting to blaming customer care whenever the evidence is unclear
redoing the work without diagnosing the cause, so the same failure returns
acceptance_tests: every complaint record shows the returned-piece photographs, the comparison against the retained file, the classification and the outcome
each complaint outcome names the upstream change made or explicitly records that none was needed
revisit_triggers: one defect class recurs after a fix was believed to be in place
complaint volume rises against a specific service class or piece type
an ambiguous case ends in a dispute the record could not resolve

base.update_signal: a recurring complaint class after a corrective change, or a dispute the retained record could not classify

edges.why_related: the mandate names the written identification of the piece as one of intake's required outputs
the images document the condition of the specific piece the written record identifies, and the ticket number ties them together
what the piece is determines which history questions matter, since a hollow locket and a solid band raise different hazards
the unknowns list is built by separating what the client reported from what the counter could actually observe
the slow photographic pass over every face is when the loupe survey finds glue lines, hairline cracks and worn-through zones
the irreplaceability class comes from the client's own account of what the piece is to them, asked during the history conversation
the liability wording has to say different things about a replaceable piece and one that no payment can restore
the decline triggers are written in the vocabulary of the feature classes the survey detects
each criterion carries the prepared sentence used to deliver that particular decline
every feature marked handled or excluded becomes a line in the in-scope or out-of-scope list
the scope is where the work is described as plating on the client's own piece rather than as making it gold
the service class chosen in the scope is what the durability conversation has to describe honestly
whether a match is even in scope, and against which reference, is settled with the rest of the scope
the date is built from the segments the agreed scope actually requires, including any outside step it implies
the signed sheet carries the wear expectation in writing so the disclosure is evidenced rather than remembered
the per-zone accept, improve or exclude decisions are exactly what the client is signing against
the gate's first confirmation is that a signed sheet exists and covers the specific risk of the step about to run
the escalation is what the gate does when its third confirmation fails because something has changed since intake
anything found and re-agreed mid-job has to be part of what is walked through and retained at collection
the complaint procedure can only classify from the retained file the handover closed and stored
the piece is tagged before it is photographed so the tag number appears in the images and ties them to the ticket
the care sheet is handed over during the guided inspection, not posted afterwards
features the counter survey misses are precisely what the bench discovers later and has to stop for
an unverifiable substrate under a worn coating is the reason a strip can open a thin zone, which is what the damage disclosure must say
the quality of the before images determines whether a later complaint can be classified at all
most wear complaints are expectation failures, so what was disclosed in writing decides how the return is answered
nothing said or written at collection may describe the finished piece as solid gold or imply a fineness claim
unresolved entitlement closes the gate: no irreversible step runs on a piece whose owner has not authorised it
the irreplaceable class converts blanket authorisation into explicit per-step client approval at the gate
a complaint class that keeps recurring on one piece type is evidence that a decline trigger is missing
complaints show which parts of the durability explanation are not landing and need rewording
what the bench keeps finding after the fact belongs on the counter feature list before the fact
the promised collection date pushes for the next step while the gate holds until its confirmations are satisfied
edges.resolution_rule: the gate wins without exception: the date moves and the client is told the same day, and no promised date ever authorises an unconfirmed irreversible step

edges.why_related: stopping to photograph, report and re-agree consumes exactly the days the promise assumed were free
edges.resolution_rule: stop-and-call wins; the shop absorbs the schedule damage, informs the client the day it happens and re-dates the job rather than proceeding to protect the date

edges.why_related: a client willing to sign anything makes it tempting to treat the signature as permission for a job the criteria decline
edges.resolution_rule: the criteria win: a signature never converts a refused job into an acceptable one, and the sheet itself states that it is not a waiver

edges.why_related: a stated liability figure invites the shop to treat exposure as bounded on a piece that money cannot restore
edges.resolution_rule: irreplaceability wins: on an irreplaceable piece the liability position is stated but never used as the reason to accept, and the refusal bar and per-step approvals govern instead

edges.why_related: the appearance the client wants and the durability they also want can pull toward different deposits and thicknesses on the same piece
edges.resolution_rule: disclose the trade openly and let the client choose one priority in writing; never promise both, and record which was chosen against the service class

edges.why_related: the care sheet is the easiest thing to point at when a complaint arrives, which biases classification toward blaming the wearer
edges.resolution_rule: evidence classifies first: the care sheet may only be cited where the wear signature actually matches use, and genuinely ambiguous cases are resolved in the client's favour once with the reason recorded

edges.why_related: both are the same bad-news conversation done well: a specific physical reason, honest options, and a recorded outcome

conflict_axes.name: counter_throughput_vs_intake_completeness
conflict_axes.description: A queue of waiting customers pushes toward a fast take-in while the evidence-and-consent gate needs photographs, a survey and a signature on every piece.
poles: accept quickly and document later
document completely before the piece enters the queue
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: documentation is the floor, not the variable: book the piece in for a proper intake slot, or take a deposit and a booking, rather than accepting an undocumented piece

conflict_axes.name: client_hopes_vs_honest_wear_truth
conflict_axes.description: Clients want to hear that the finish will last for years and look like solid gold; the mechanism supports neither promise on a coating over a used piece.
poles: tell the client what closes the sale
state the mechanism and its limits in writing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honesty wins every time: describe the mechanism, offer the heavier specification as the real answer to durability, and accept losing the sale rather than making a claim the shop cannot keep

conflict_axes.name: revenue_now_vs_refusal_discipline
conflict_axes.description: A quiet week and a valuable-looking job argue for taking work the written criteria decline.
poles: take the job and manage the risk
apply the decline list as written
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the criteria dominate revenue and goodwill; log the refusal so the shop can see honestly what its criteria cost and decide about capability later, in calm conditions

conflict_axes.name: promised_date_vs_approval_gates
conflict_axes.description: Approval gates and stop-and-calls consume days the promised date did not contain, especially when the client is unreachable.
poles: keep the promised date
hold at the gate until confirmed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the gate holds and the date moves; capture a second contact and a stated fallback preference at intake so unreachable clients cost hours rather than weeks

conflict_axes.name: client_account_vs_bench_verification
conflict_axes.description: The client's confident history of the piece competes with what the bench can actually verify before an irreversible step.
poles: rely on the client's account
treat every claim as unverified until checked
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record the account as a claim and plan the verification; where verification is impossible, the unknown is disclosed and accepted in writing or the job is declined

conflict_axes.name: sentimental_value_vs_liability_limit
conflict_axes.description: The shop's liability position can be stated in money, but the pieces most likely to generate a claim are the ones money cannot replace.
poles: manage exposure with a stated liability basis
manage exposure by not accepting the piece
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for the irreplaceable class the liability statement is disclosure, not protection; the real controls are the refusal bar, the conservative process option and per-step approval

conflict_axes.name: counter_friction_vs_dispute_defence
conflict_axes.description: Every additional form, photograph and signature protects the shop later and costs warmth and time now.
poles: keep the counter light and friendly
capture everything that a dispute would need
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep a small fixed core that never flexes (tag, photos, scope, signature) and let depth scale with declared value, irreplaceability and irreversibility

conflict_axes.name: process_defect_vs_wearer_behaviour
conflict_axes.description: When a piece comes back marked, the same evidence can be read as a shop failure or as use the care sheet warned against.
poles: defend the shop's work
own the defect and fix it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: classify from the wear signature and the retained file before any answer is given; resolve genuine ambiguity in the client's favour once and record it so the pattern is visible

conflict_axes.name: batching_efficiency_vs_custody_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Running several clients' similar pieces together is how a small shop makes the economics work, and it is also how pieces become unidentifiable.
poles: batch for gold and time efficiency
keep every customer piece individually identified
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: custody integrity wins on customer pieces: batch only in numbered single-job carriers, and let the pricing knowledge base handle the economics of the smaller batch

conflict_axes.name: evidence_retention_vs_data_minimisation
conflict_axes.description: Complete job files with images and contact details are what make disputes decidable, and they are also personal data the shop must justify holding.
poles: retain everything indefinitely
hold as little as possible for as short as possible
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: define a stated retention period tied to the dispute window, keep the file as one unit with controlled access, and verify the privacy rules that apply in the shop's own jurisdiction

edge_cases.description: A brooch set with pearls and an opal arrives for a full refresh and the client refuses to have the stones unset, since the setting is original
edge_cases.trigger: heat- and chemistry-sensitive stones cannot be removed and cannot safely stay
edge_cases.mitigation: offer a reduced scope that excludes the stone-bearing area from immersion and heat if the shop has a method it trusts, otherwise decline with the prepared sentence and refer to a setter who can unset and reset

edge_cases.description: A client brings in a piece they describe as solid gold, and the counter can see plating worn through to a different-coloured base at the contact points
edge_cases.trigger: the piece contradicts the owner's belief about what it is
edge_cases.mitigation: describe only what is observed on the piece, avoid pronouncing on what it is, refer the client to a qualified appraiser for identification, and write the work order as plating on the client's piece with no fineness claim

edge_cases.description: A partner drops off a ring on the owner's behalf and asks for an inscription to be polished out at the same time
edge_cases.trigger: the bearer requests an irreversible change they may not be entitled to authorise
edge_cases.mitigation: record owner and bearer separately, accept the reversible part of the job if any, and hold the inscription request until the owner authorises it directly

edge_cases.description: A daily-worn ring is already through to base metal on the underside of the shank and the client wants it looking new
edge_cases.trigger: a worn-through zone that stripping or polishing may thin further or open
edge_cases.mitigation: photograph the zone at macro range, disclose in writing that it may open during strip or polish, offer referral for a re-shank first, and record the client's accept, improve or exclude decision before any gate is opened

edge_cases.description: A client asks the shop to write gold on the receipt because they intend to sell the piece online
edge_cases.trigger: a request for paperwork that would help a plated piece be resold as solid
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the wording with the standard sentence, state plainly what the shop will write instead, and decline the job entirely if the purpose depends on the misrepresentation

edge_cases.description: Old soft solder appears under the stripped coating on a piece the client said had never been repaired
edge_cases.trigger: a bench discovery that contradicts the intake account and changes the heat and chemistry risk
edge_cases.mitigation: stop before the next step, photograph the seam in place, contact the client with the options including return part-worked, and record the agreed option before resuming

edge_cases.description: The client cannot be reached for two weeks and their piece sits stripped and unfinished
edge_cases.trigger: an approval gate that no one can pass because the client is unavailable
edge_cases.mitigation: store the piece in its numbered carrier in the secure class with its state photographed, document every contact attempt, and change intake to capture a second contact and a stated fallback preference for this exact situation

edge_cases.description: A piece cannot be located in the shop at the end of a busy day
edge_cases.trigger: a break in the custody chain between stations
edge_cases.mitigation: stop other work and search by the station log immediately, tell the client the same day rather than after the search succeeds or fails, and treat any recurrence as a mandate to change the tagging scheme rather than to try harder

edge_cases.description: A client returns months later saying the plating wore off within a week, with no images of their own
edge_cases.trigger: a late complaint that rests entirely on recollection
edge_cases.mitigation: re-intake the piece under full photo discipline, classify the wear signature against the retained before, after and disclosure records, and answer from that comparison rather than from the strength of the claim

edge_cases.description: A client mentions that the piece makes their skin react and asks whether plating will make it safe to wear
edge_cases.trigger: a health question arriving inside a commercial intake conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: give no safety assurance at the counter, route the question to the nickel-release and skin-contact obligation classes owned by the compliance specialist and to the client's own clinician, and decline the job if it can only proceed on an implied health claim

edge_cases.description: One earring of a matched pair is brought in for refresh and the client intends to wear the pair together
edge_cases.trigger: partial treatment of a set that will be worn as a set
edge_cases.mitigation: state at intake that the treated item will outshine its partner, offer to treat both, agree a physical reference and viewing light if only one is treated, and record the choice in the scope statement

edge_cases.description: An estate lot arrives with several family members claiming a say in what happens to the pieces
edge_cases.trigger: authorisation is contested among multiple claimants
edge_cases.mitigation: accept instructions only from the executor or an agreed single representative, hold irreversible steps until that is settled in writing, and return the lot unworked if it is not

workflow.action: Set the intake mandate and who may accept a piece
workflow.description: Write down the artifacts intake must produce and name the person accountable for the accept or refuse decision
workflow.artifact: intake policy sheet posted at the counter
workflow.gate: the four required outputs and the accountable acceptor are named in writing

workflow.action: Take custody and tag the piece
workflow.description: Assign the ticket number, tag the piece, count small parts and place it in its own numbered carrier
workflow.artifact: tagged piece, client receipt and opened ticket carrying the same number
workflow.gate: tag, receipt, ticket and small-part count agree before the piece leaves the counter

workflow.description: Record form, dimensions, mass, stone count and construction features, with marks recorded as marks
workflow.artifact: written piece description on the ticket
workflow.gate: the description distinguishes this piece from any similar piece and asserts no metal conclusion

workflow.description: Photograph every face plus a macro of each defect, before any cleaning, with the tag in frame
workflow.artifact: dated before-image set attached to the ticket
workflow.gate: every recorded defect has a macro image and every image ties to the ticket number

workflow.description: Ask the prior-plating, prior-repair, glue, wear-pattern, exposure and skin-reaction questions and record the answers as the client's account
workflow.artifact: history answers on the ticket with unknowns recorded as unknown
workflow.gate: all history questions are answered or explicitly marked unknown, and no skin-safety assurance was given

workflow.action: Record what cannot be verified at the counter
workflow.description: Separate observed from claimed from unknown and attach a verification step or an accepted-risk note to each unknown
workflow.gate: no unknown has silently become an assumption anywhere else on the ticket

workflow.action: Survey the risk features under a loupe
workflow.description: Work the feature list for stones, glue, hollows, enamel, mechanisms, prior repairs, mixed metals and worn-through zones
workflow.artifact: completed feature checklist with a decision per flag
workflow.gate: every flagged feature carries a handled, excluded or stopped decision

workflow.action: Classify irreplaceability and record the declared value
workflow.description: Ask whether the piece could be replaced at all, record the class, then record the client's declared value and the handling class it selects
workflow.artifact: class and declared value on the ticket
workflow.gate: the class is recorded from the client's own answer and the elevated handling it triggers is noted

workflow.description: Test the assembled picture against the written decline list and either accept or decline
workflow.artifact: accept or decline decision recorded with its criterion
workflow.gate: no accepted job matches a criterion, and every decline names the criterion and the alternative offered

workflow.description: State in the client's language what will be done and, at equal length, what will not
workflow.artifact: in-scope and out-of-scope statement on the ticket
workflow.gate: the out-of-scope section names the defects that will remain and the components not touched

workflow.action: Give the disclosures and take the signature
workflow.description: Walk the wear mechanism, the not-solid-gold statement, the per-zone damage decisions, the colour reference and the date, then sign
workflow.artifact: signed risk acknowledgment referencing the ticket and photo set
workflow.gate: the sheet is signed before any bench work, contains no time guarantee and states that it is not a waiver of the refusal criteria

workflow.description: Compare before and after images with the client, walk the scope including exclusions, reconcile counts, hand over the care sheet and take acceptance
workflow.artifact: acceptance record and complete retained job file
workflow.gate: counts reconcile, the after set is comparable to the before set, and the acceptance signature and care sheet issue are recorded

dominance_rules.rule: Refusal criteria dominate revenue, diary pressure and any client waiver
dominance_rules.rationale: no single job is worth an irreplaceable loss, and a signature cannot restore a destroyed heirloom
dominance_rules.trigger: an assembled intake picture matches a written decline trigger
dominance_rules.action: decline using the prepared sentence, log the criterion and offer the alternative or referral

dominance_rules.rule: The safety and compliance verdict dominates client wishes, scope and schedule
dominance_rules.rationale: chemical handling, waste and marking obligations sit above commercial preference, and the compliance specialist is the gate for them
dominance_rules.trigger: a requested job or wording touches a chemical, waste or marking obligation class
dominance_rules.action: route to the compliance specialist and treat a block as final regardless of what the client wants or has paid

dominance_rules.rule: The never-solid-gold rule dominates any wording a client or the shop's own sales instinct prefers
dominance_rules.rationale: misrepresenting plated work is a dishonesty the shop can never recover from, and it can travel into a resale the shop enabled
dominance_rules.trigger: any speech, receipt, label or advertisement that would describe or imply plated work as solid gold
dominance_rules.action: use the standard correcting sentence, refuse the wording, and decline the job if its purpose depends on the misrepresentation

dominance_rules.rule: The approval gate dominates the promised date
dominance_rules.rationale: an unrecoverable step taken to protect a date destroys the piece and the relationship together
dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible step is due while any of the gate's confirmations is unsatisfied
dominance_rules.action: hold the piece, inform the client the same day and re-date the job

dominance_rules.rule: Documented condition evidence dominates anyone's recollection
dominance_rules.rationale: memory is not evidence and the commonest dispute is about when a flaw appeared
dominance_rules.trigger: a disagreement about the state of a piece at intake or handover
dominance_rules.action: decide from the dated images and the signed scope, and if the evidence is missing treat the gap as the shop's

dominance_rules.rule: Irreplaceability dominates declared value in every handling decision
dominance_rules.rationale: money can settle a claim but cannot return the object, so exposure on these pieces is controlled by not risking them
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece is classed irreplaceable regardless of the value written on the ticket
dominance_rules.action: apply the higher refusal bar, the conservative process option and explicit per-step client approval

dominance_rules.rationale: almost every intake mistake in this trade is an unverified belief written down as a fact
dominance_rules.trigger: the counter cannot verify substrate, prior repair or construction before an irreversible step
dominance_rules.action: record it as unknown with a verification step or a written accepted risk, and never let it become an assumption in the scope, the date or the disclosure

dominance_rules.rule: Custody integrity dominates batching convenience on customer pieces
dominance_rules.rationale: a piece that cannot be identified after stripping is a loss no efficiency gain can offset
dominance_rules.trigger: a temptation to run several clients' similar pieces together without individual carriers
dominance_rules.action: keep numbered single-job carriers and let the batching economics be handled as a pricing question

dominance_rules.rationale: an unwritten disclosure is indistinguishable at complaint time from one that never happened
dominance_rules.trigger: any wear, damage, colour or timeline expectation being set at the counter
dominance_rules.action: put it on the signed sheet before work starts and treat anything missing from the sheet as not disclosed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Photograph the piece before any cleaning, polishing or handling at the bench
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the loss of arrival-state evidence, which turns every later condition question into an unwinnable argument

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag the piece and open the ticket before it leaves the counter
anti_rework_rules.prevents: identity loss once stripping removes the finish that made the piece recognisable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the loupe feature survey before writing the scope statement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scope agreed and priced against features that turn out to need exclusion, forcing a re-agreement mid-job

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record unknowns as unknown before promising any outcome or date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an assumption propagating into the scope, the disclosure and the timeline, all of which must then be rewritten

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask the prior-repair and glued-component questions before any heat or immersion decision
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering soft solder or a released component at the bench, when the only options left are damage control

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm entitlement before accepting a job containing an irreversible step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: permanent work performed on someone else's piece on an authorisation that was never theirs to give

anti_rework_rules.rule: Take the signature before the first irreversible step, never at collection
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a disclosure that legally and practically never happened, and a job that cannot be defended

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree and retain a physical colour reference and its viewing light at intake
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a re-plate to chase a remembered colour that no record can settle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Walk the out-of-scope list at handover with the images in view
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a complaint days later about a defect the client agreed to leave, which then costs a redo to resolve

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint arrives on a delivered job
iteration_protocol.action: re-intake the piece under full photo discipline, classify against the retained file, resolve, and record which upstream document changes as a result

iteration_protocol.trigger: the bench repeatedly discovers conditions the counter survey should have caught
iteration_protocol.action: add the missed feature class to the loupe survey and to the history questions, and re-brief whoever accepts pieces

iteration_protocol.trigger: a job is stopped and returned after an irreversible step had already started
iteration_protocol.action: move the criterion that stopped it earlier into the intake decision so the same case is caught at the counter next time

iteration_protocol.trigger: clients are unreachable at approval gates often enough to strand part-worked pieces
iteration_protocol.action: capture a second contact and a stated fallback preference at intake, and add a holding-state photograph and storage class for stranded jobs

iteration_protocol.trigger: marking, consumer-protection or privacy rules in the shop's jurisdiction change
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected wording with the compliance specialist and the shop's own counsel, and re-date the forms in use

iteration_protocol.trigger: a piece is mislaid, misidentified or damaged in the shop
iteration_protocol.action: audit the custody chain from the station log, change the tagging or carrier scheme rather than exhorting more care, and tell the client the same day

iteration_protocol.trigger: colour disputes recur even where a reference was agreed
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the reference procedure, record the viewing light explicitly and retain the reference with the job through to handover

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because nothing can be documented, assessed or refused until intake has a mandate, a custody chain and a written identification of the piece; the assessment units (photographs, history, unknowns, feature survey, irreplaceability, declared value, entitlement) come next because every accept-or-refuse judgement is made from what they produce; the decision units (refusal criteria, refusal delivery, scope) sit above them because they consume the assessment and determine whether and in what form the job exists; the expectation units (never solid gold, wear, pre-existing damage, colour, turnaround) follow the scope because each of them describes an agreed job honestly rather than a hypothetical one; the authorisation units (signed acknowledgment, irreversible-step gate, stop-and-call) come after every disclosure exists because their whole function is to check that what is about to happen matches what was agreed; and the closeout units come last because handover, aftercare and complaint handling compose all of the earlier evidence into a job that can be defended and into the feedback that improves the next intake.
